grand_strategy.reading:
Cyprus runs the grand strategy of a small member state of the EU that is also half
an occupied island: it cannot change facts on the ground, so it multiplies the
number of actors whose interests are tied to the island and hopes that one of them
will, in the end, move Turkey. The EU is the main multiplier (membership, the
presidency, the veto on SAFE and the customs union), the Greek-French-Israeli-US
ring is the second (air defence, arms, drills), gas is the third (Egypt, Israel,
Greece, Chevron, Eni). Each of them works, and each of them has a Luttwak cost:
the veto gives Ankara a grievance, the ring gives it a pretext, the gas makes
Cyprus a client of Cairo and Jerusalem, and the bases that tie Britain and the
United States to the island are the ones that drew Iranian-made drones onto it on
1-4 March 2026. The year's two facts pull in opposite directions: the election of
Erhurman (19 Oct 2025, 62.8%) and a UN track that is moving, against a Turkey that
is more entrenched in the EU's defence and trade files and a Gaza-and-Iran war
that has made Cyprus a front-line state. Two signals that are not rows: Guterres
leaves office on 31 Dec 2026, so Nicosia has a deadline it did not set, and the
president's own praise for Trump ('you know where you stand') comes with a defence
budget cut at home. The north is not an actor in the atlas: it is recorded through
Turkey's stance, rows and troop presence, not as a territory with its own grade.

stances.note: Mirrors Turkey's own stance (rival, grievance) and the evidence its card holds. Turkey keeps troops in the north, does not recognise the Republic and defends a two-state, 'sovereign equality' settlement; the Republic claims sovereignty over the whole island but controls only the south, and the Turkish Cypriot north is not an actor in the atlas, so it is recorded here, through Turkey, and not as claimed territory. Rival, not adversary: neither wants the other state's end, and a live UN track exists (Guterres on the island 27-29 Jul 2026; leaders' meetings with Erhurman, elected 19 Oct 2025 over the Ankara-backed Tatar; Guterres considering a three-way meeting, 24 Sep). Cyprus and Turkey are not NATO co-members (Turkey blocks Cyprus's PfP route), so the reluctant_ally rule does not apply. Stable: Cyprus keeps vetoing Turkey's SAFE access and the customs-union upgrade; Guterres leaves office on 31 Dec 2026. Bond - grievance: 1974.

stances_toward.note: Turkey does not recognise the Republic of Cyprus and keeps troops in the north; the settlement formula it defends is 'sovereign equality' and two states. Rival, not adversary: the two are not in NATO together (so the reluctant_ally rule does not apply) and there is a live UN track - Guterres visited 27-29 Jul 2026, Christodoulides and the Turkish Cypriot leader Erhurman (elected in autumn 2025 on a unification platform, defeating the Turkey-backed Tatar) met on 26 Aug, 9 Sep and 17 Sep, and Ankara has not rejected the UN's proposals but is said to be seeking EU concessions in exchange. Stable: no joint meeting of the guarantors is planned, and Guterres leaves office at the end of 2026. Bond - grievance.

relations_to.summary: Great Sea Interconnector: a 1,208 km, 525 kV HVDC cable linking Crete, Cyprus and later Israel (1 GW, expandable to 2 GW), cost about EUR 1.9bn, EUR 657m from the EU's Connecting Europe Facility for Crete-Cyprus. Meridiam took 66% of the project company on 5 Aug 2026 (IPTO keeps 34% and the technical lead; Nexans lays the cable). Surveys have been frozen since a Turkish naval standoff off Kasos in July 2024; about 60% are done; a NAVTEX could allow restart in October and Gerapetritis said work could resume before the end of 2026. Nicosia has asked for fresh viability studies before paying more.
